newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee fireworks warehouse blast kills four.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee fireworks warehouse blast kills four.

text.p: Four people were killed and several injured on Thursday when a fireworks factory warehouse exploded, scattering live shells for blocks and causing widespread damage, officials said.
The dead included two teenaged girls working inside the warehouse, a man whose truck exploded at a loading dock and a second man found in rubble outside the building.
Charles Winfrey, news editor of the La Follette Press, the town's weekly newspaper, said the other injuries were comparatively minor and officials did not expect to find more victims.

The toll might have been higher had the blast not occurred at lunch time when some workers had left the building, police said. It was not known how many people were working at the warehouse earlier in the day.

Winfrey said the blast knocked out windows and caved in a door at the Midway Baptist Church across the street from the warehouse. He also said there was severe structural damage to a fellowship hall being built next to the church.
"One house caught fire but it was put out," he added.
Victor Jennings, who works at WQLA Radio in La Follette, said, said the windows in a car dealership a mile and a half away were blown out.
He said hundreds of live shells were strewn about and the fire department sprayed water on them to prevent more explosions.

The warehouse, on the edge of the town of 9,000 about 30 miles (48 kms) north of Knoxville in northeast Tennessee, belonged to Pyro Shows Inc., which calls itself "an international leader in the pyrotechnic field." It put on the 1995 Fourth of July fireworks show in Washington, D.C.
